label: NOTE: a three-phase cadence with two DIFFERENT end comparisons, and the fixture is built to separate them. Cases land exactly ON each boundary as well as either side of it; whole cadences are driven block by block with lengths that are and are not multiples of the block; and the tone OBJECT is compared byte for byte after every call, which is the only observable that can see the generator running (or not running) during a phase whose output is all zeros. Six degenerate shapes -- zero count, negative count, zero and negative lengths -- are in the first section.
the tone phase ends one sample early, which agrees except when elapsed + count lands exactly on TONE_LEN
the silence phase ends one sample early, which is the tone phase's comparison and not its own
the tone phase measures itself against the silence length
the silence phase measures itself against the tone length
the counter is tested before the block is added to it
the tone phase carries its overrun into the silence instead of zeroing it
the silence phase carries its overrun rather than zeroing it
the tone phase advances straight to the done phase
the silence phase wraps round to the tone phase instead of stopping
the phase is incremented rather than assigned, which agrees for every phase the object can reach and not for a corrupt one
why: The assignment it rewrites is inside the arm guarded by `phase == V32ANS_PHASE_TONE`, so `phase` is 0 there and `phase + 1` is 1, which IS V32ANS_PHASE_SILENCE.  No input can separate them: the only way to enter that arm with a different `phase` is for the guard to be wrong, and a separate mutation covers the guard.  Registered rather than deleted because the object ASSIGNS -- `movl $0x1,0x4(%ebx)` at 0x86860, an immediate and not an increment -- so if the arm ever gains a second entry condition this stops being equivalent and will be reported MIScounted.
